title: WPSS/627/2021 of SONU KUMAR Vs DEFENCE MINISTRY GOVERNMENT OF INDIA NEW DELHI
quotes: J. (Through Video Conferencing) Mr. Anshu Kumar, Advocate for the petitioner. The brief facts, which are apparent from the records of the Writ Petition are that the father of the petitioner late Mr. Chandra Pal, who was serving with the respondents, had met with the said demise as back as on 10th June, 2010. Ever since, the death of the bread winner of the family, none of the dependants of late Mr. Chandra Pal, had ever applied for the grant of compassionate appointment, as per the Cantonment Board Funds Rules, 1937. In fact, if the pleading of the Writ Petition is taken into consideration, the application for the compassionate appointment was made by the petitioner on 13th May, 2021, which was almost after 11 years of death of late Mr. Chandra Pal. Under the Rules itself, and as per the memorandum, which was just read over by the counsel for the petitioner, the upper time limit provided under th

ars, which is subject to relaxation to the maximum period of 7 years. But, however, still the memorandum leaves a scope that further extension could be granted only under exceptional circumstances. I am of the view that the third aspect of the memorandum of granting a relaxation beyond the period of time limit of 7 years, from the date of death, has had to be on some exceptional circumstances. In this case, the petitioner himself has applied for compassionate appointment after 11 years of death and even beyond 7 years, i.e. maximum time period which have been or could have been relaxed under the office memorandum. There is another logic behind it. That is, that the provisions of compassionate appointment takes the shape of welfare legislation, in order to meet the emergent and sudden crisis which the family suffers on account of sudden death of the bread winner. To tide away that difficulty, the p
tail: ons of compassionate appointment takes the shape of welfare legislation, in order to meet the emergent and sudden crisis which the family suffers on account of sudden death of the bread winner. To tide away that difficulty, the provisions for compassionate appointment has been legislated in different departments and the appointment has had to be sought within the certain specified time frame, as framed and provided under the law itself applicable to it, and that period cannot be stretched to an infinity, because the presumption would be that, once the family has survived for last 11 years after the death of the bread winner, as it is in the present case, there was no emergent exigency for consideration of appointment on compassionate grounds and hence, delayed application of the petitioner, as was filed on 13th May, 2021, after 11 years of death was even contrary to their own office memorandum which was read over by the counsel for the petitioner. quotes: Justice Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J. delivered the following judgment: JUDGMENT This Special Appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 06.08.2020, passed by the learned Single Judge, in Writ Petition (S/S) No.2120 of 2019. 2. By the impugned judgment dated 06.08.2020, the learned Single Judge has directed the appellants (respondent nos.2 and 3 in the writ petition) to consider the case of the respondent-writ petitioner for appointment on compassionate ground in accordance with the policy existing prior to 12.06.2018, within a period of three months from the date of production of a certified copy of the order. The learned Single Judge has relied upon a judgment rendered by a Division Bench of this Court in Special Appeal No.38 of 2020, wherein it has been held that the ban imposed on compassionate appointment vide Government Order date 12.06.2018 will not apply retrospectively to cases wher

12.06.2018 will not apply retrospectively to cases where application seeking compassionate appointment was made earlier. 3. Learned Senior Counsel for the appellants, has placed reliance upon a judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of "N.C. Santosh vs. State of Karnataka", passed in Civil Appeal Nos.9280-9281 of 2014 on 04.03.2020, wherein it has been held that the norms prevailing on the date of consideration of application seeking compassionate appointment shall govern the field and the norms prevailing on the date of death will have not application. Learned Senior Counsel for the 3 appellants, thus, submits that the judgment passed by the learned Single Judge is flawed and needs to be interfered with. 4. Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record. 5. From perusal of the record, it is apparent that the death of writ petitioner's father had occurred on 13.12.2017 an
tail: of "N.C. Santosh vs. State of Karnataka", passed in Civil Appeal 4 Nos.9280-9281 of 2014 on 04.03.2020, does not support the case of the appellants, as the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the said judgment held that it is the date of consideration of application, which is relevant for deciding which norms will apply to a particular case. The new policy banning compassionate appointment was enforced much later on 12.06.2018. Therefore, it will not have any retrospective operation. 8. Even otherwise also, no positive direction has been issued by the learned Single Judge to the employer (appellants herein) to appoint the writ petitioner on compassionate ground. The direction issued is to consider the claim of the writ petitioner in accordance with law, with the rider that the ban imposed by Government Order dated 12.06.2018 will not apply in the case of the writ petitioner. 9. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case, we do not find any illegality in the order passed by the learned Single Judge that calls for any interference. Accordingly, the Special Appeal fails and is, accordingly, dismissed. 10. No costs. (Raghvendra Singh Chauhan, C.J.) (Manoj Kumar Tiwari, J.) NISHANT

After his fatherís death, the petitioner, being the only son, moved an application before the authority concerned on 23.04.2007 seeking appointment on compassionate grounds. Said application was rejected by the Secretary, Government of Uttarakhand, vide letter dated 23.10.2010, stating that under the provisions of Uttarakhand U.P. Recruitment of Dependents of Government Servants Dying in Harness Rules, 1974 and Uttaranchal (the Uttar Pradesh Recruitment of Dependents of Government Servant Dying in Harness Rules, 1974) Adaptation and Amendment Order 2002 and First Amendment 2004 adopted by State of Uttara
tail: ing from any lacunae, therefore, the adoption deed which is a registered deed, cannot be said to be bad or against the provisions of the Hindu Law. Insofar as the date of adoption of the petitioner is concerned, the contents of the adoption deed would reveal that the petitioner was adopted by the deceased employee and his wife 20 years back, i.e. before the death of the deceased employee. Thus, it is evidently clear that on the date of death of 8 the deceased employee, the petitioner was legally adopted son of the deceased employee. That being the position, this Court is of the considered view that the respondent has wrongly denied the claim of the petitioner for compassionate appointment on the ground that he is the adopted son. 11. In view of the foregoing discussion, the writ petition is allowed. Impugned order dated 23.03.2010 is hereby quashed. The respondents are directed to re-consider the case of the petitioner for appointment on compassionate grounds, in light of the observations made hereinabove, commensurate to his qualification, in their department, within three months from the date of production of a certified copy of this judgment. tail: at she is dependent on her husband; and merely the 'No Objection Certificate' issued by her brother and mother in her favour, would not entitle the appellant-writ petitioner to get the compassionate appointment. Learned Counsel for the appellant/writ petitioner urged the same grounds, which were taken before the learned Single Judge. No, doubt, the intent and purpose of dying in harness scheme is to provide a helping hand to the family, which has all of a sudden lost the sole breadwinner, so that the death of an individual does not become an economic death of his family. But the basic test under the scheme is the dependence of the family member on the deceased government servant at the time of his demise. As noted hereinabove, it is the pleaded case of the appellant-writ petitioner herself that she is dependent on her husband, and since the matter stood thus, we are satisfied that the order under appeal does not necessitate any interference by this Court in the present intra-Court appeal. tail: 's application for compassionate appointment, inasmuch as, he did not consider the law laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case V. Sivamurty Vs State of Andhra Pradesh & others reported in (2008) 13 SCC 730. I have gone through the judgment referred by learned counsel for the petitioner. In that judgment there was a policy formulated by the State Government to grant compassionate appointment to dependants of employees, who retire on medical ground, which was struck down by the High Court as unconstitutional. The matter was taken up in appeal and in that background, Hon'ble Supreme Court held that compassionate appointment cannot be restricted to the death in harness cases. Since in that case, there was a policy framed by the employer, whereas in the present case there is no such policy, therefore, said judgment is clearly distinguishable of facts, therefore, this Court, while exercising power of judicial review cannot ask the respondents to do something which is not permissible under their policy. In such view of the matter, there is no scope of interference in the present matter. Accordingly, writ petition fails and is hereby dismissed. (Manoj K. Tiwari, J.) 02.05.2019 Aswal

title: WPSS/3035/2018 of Deepak Kashyap Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS
quotes: WPSS No. 3035 of 2018 Hon'ble Manoj K. Tiwari, J. Mr. Niranjan Bhatt, Advocate for the petitioner. Mr. N.P. Sah, Standing Counsel for the State of Uttarakhand. Heard learned counsel for the parties. Petitioner's mother Smt. Neelam Devi was serving as constable in 40th P.A.C. Haridwar, who died on 13.11.2016 while in service. Petitioner applied for compassionate appointment under the provisions of Dying-in-Harness Rules, 1974. Petitioner's application has been rejected by the Commandant, 40th Battalion, P.A.C., Haridwar vide order dated 10.10.2017. Feeling aggrieved by rejection of his claim for compassionate appointment, petitioner has approached this Court. A Perusal of the rejection order dated 10.10.2017 reveals that petitioner's claim has been rejected with total non application of mind. In the

etitioner has approached this Court. A Perusal of the rejection order dated 10.10.2017 reveals that petitioner's claim has been rejected with total non application of mind. In the rejection order, it is stated that there is no provision for providing employment under the Dying-in-Harness Rules, 1974. It is further stated that petitioner's claim for compassionate appointment is closed in view of the instructions received from Police Headquarters. Dying-in-Harness Rules have been framed in exercise of powers under proviso to Article 309 of the Constitution. Rule 3 of the said Rules provides that the said Rules shall apply to all public services and posts in connection with the affairs of the State of Uttarakhand except services and posts which are within the purview of Public Service Commission. Rule 4 of the said Rules gives overriding effect to the provision contained in these Rules. Rule 5 of the said
tail: ent causes undue hardship in any particular case, it may dispense with or relax the requirement as it may consider necessary for dealing with the case in a just and equitable manner. (2) As far as possible, such an employment should be given in the same department in which the deceased Government servant was employed prior to his death." In view of the specific provisions contained in Dying-in-Harness Rules, 1974 the stand taken by the Commandant (respondent no. 3) for rejecting petitioner's claim cannot be sustained in the eyes of law. These Rules are statutory in nature, which shall have overriding effect over the Government Orders/ executive instructions issued by the State Government. Thus, the reliance placed by Commandant 40th Battalion on the instructions issued by the Police Headquarters is legally unsustainable. In such view of the matter, the writ petition is allowed. Impugned order dated 10.10.2017 is quashed. The Commandant, 40th Battalion P.A.C., Haridwar is directed to re-consider petitioner's claim for compassionate appointment in accordance with law within eight weeks from the date of production of certified copy of this order. (Manoj K. Tiwari, J.) Navin 01.04.2019

title: CRLR/130/2013 of Mukandi Lal AND ANOTHER Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND ANOTHER
quotes: CRLR No. 130 of 2013 Hon'ble Alok Singh, J. Mr. D.C.S. Rawat, Advocate for the revisionists. Mr. Bhuvnesh Joshi, Advocate for the respondent no. 2. Revisionists are father-in-law and mother-in-law of respondent no. 2. Son of revisionists was died on 16.02.2004. After his death, respondent no. 2 got service on compassionate ground. Revisionists claimed maintenance under Section 125 CrPC against respondent no. 2. Parties entered into compromise. Suit filed by the revisionists was disposed of in terms of compromise. Thereafter, respondent no. 2 got married with another man. She filed a Misc. Case No. 5 of 2011 under Section 127 CrPC, which was allowed by the Sessions Court and directed that revisionists will not be entitled for any maintenance. Feeling aggrieved,
tail: es entered into compromise. Suit filed by the revisionists was disposed of in terms of compromise. Thereafter, respondent no. 2 got married with another man. She filed a Misc. Case No. 5 of 2011 under Section 127 CrPC, which was allowed by the Sessions Court and directed that revisionists will not be entitled for any maintenance. Feeling aggrieved, revisionists approached this Court. Mr. D.C.S. Rawat, Advocate for the revisionists submits that since the order of maintenance was passed on the basis of compromise, therefore, case under Section 127 CrPC was not maintainable. Mr. Bhuvnesh Joshi, Advocate for respondent no. 2 submits that the relation between revisionists and respondent no. 2 came to an end, when respondent no. 2 got married with another man. I am not convinced with the argument of Mr. D.C.S. Rawat, Advocate. Under Section 125 CrPC maintenance can be given to wife, children and parents. Former father-in-law and mother-in-law are not covered under the provision of Section 125 CrPC. Therefore, order of maintenance was void. Tiwari, J. 1. Petitioner is widow of Late Anil Singh, who was a regular employee of General Reserve Engineering Force (in short ëGREFí) and died while in service on 28.09.2010. In view of the precarious financial condition of the family, petitioner applied for compassionate appointment to GREF in terms of the applicable Scheme. Under the said Scheme, 5% of total vacancies in a given year alone are available to be filled by compassionate appointment. Since large number of applications are received seeking compassionate appointment and number of vacancy are very less compared to number of applications, therefore, a high powered committee was constituted to assess the comparative hardship of the applicants. The sai

mpared to number of applications, therefore, a high powered committee was constituted to assess the comparative hardship of the applicants. The said committee considered petitionerís claim and recommended her for compassionate appointment. However, her candidature was rejected by the Competent Authority/Commandant GREF Centre vide order dated 07.10.2016 only on the ground that petitioner was 321⁄2 years of age, when she submitted application for compassionate appointment. 2. The Scheme for Compassionate Appointment, relied upon by the respondents, is part of record as annexure No. 2 to the counter affidavit. Para 6-B of the said Scheme deals with ëRelaxationsí and provides that upper age limit could be relaxed wherever found necessary, however, lower age limit cannot be relaxed below 18 years of age. 3. Based on the said stipulation in the Scheme, Mr. Niranjan Bhatt, learned counsel for the petiti
tail: a dependant of deceased employee in order to help his family to tide over sudden financial crisis caused due to the untimely death of sole breadwinner. He further submits that there is no upper age limit for grant of compassionate appointment, as is apparent from para 6-B of the Scheme. 4. This Court finds substance in the submission of learned counsel for the petitioner. The Scheme for Compassionate Appointment is a benevolent Scheme, which has to be construed liberally. Moreover, para 6-B of the said scheme specifically provides that compassionate appointment cannot be denied to a person merely on the ground that he/she has become overage. 5. In such view of the matter, rejection of petitionerís claim for appointment on the ground that she has become overage cannot be sustained in the eyes of law. 6. Accordingly, writ petition is allowed. The impugned order dated 07.10.2016 is quashed. The Competent Authority/Commandant, GREF Centre Dighi Camp, Pune is directed to re-consider petitionerís claim in the light of the applicable Scheme for Compassionate Appointment, within four months from the date of production of certified copy of this order. (Manoj K. Tiwari, J.) 18.03.2019 Aswal

quotes: Writ Petition No. 1211 of 2010 (S/S) Rakesh Kumar .....Petitioner Versus Union of India and others ....Respondents Advocate : Mr. Sanjeev Singh, Advocate for the petitioner Mr. Lalit Sharma, Standing Counsel for the Union of India Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J. The petitioner in the present writ petition has challenged the impugned order dated 30.10.2009, as passed by the respondent No. 2, whereby the claim of the petitioner for appointment on compassionate grounds has been rejected. The petitioner has further sought a relief that his claim for appointment on compassionate ground may be directed to be considered in accordance with the educational qualifications, which he possesses. 2. The brief facts leading to the filing of the present writ petition are that the father of the petitioner who was employed in the Military Engineering Service (M.E.S.) Roorkee as a Mate Carpenter had met with the sa

vice (M.E.S.) Roorkee as a Mate Carpenter had met with the sad demise on 09.11.2002. As a matter of fact, it is admitted that after the death of his father on 09.11.2002, the elder brother of the petitioner - Mange Ram had filed an application seeking compassionate appointment by moving an application on 21.02.2005; but later on he withdrew his candidature and thereafter petitioner has extended his candidature to be considered for appointment on compassionate grounds by filing of the application only on 20.09.2006. The application of the petitioner for being appointed on compassionate grounds was considered by respondent No. 2, along with various such other applications of other candidates which have been submitted for appointment on compassionate grounds. Ultimately, the application of the petitioner had been rejected by the impugned order dated 30.10.2009 on the ground that as per the conditions
tail: no latitude can be extended to grant a compassionate appointment because it has been held out in catena of judgements of various Courts including the Hon'ble Apex Court that the consideration of appointment on compassionate grounds cannot be claimed as matter of right, but rather it is a compassion which has been expressed to the family which has been deprived of the breadwinner of the said family. This aspect of delayed applying too would disentitle the petitioner for compassionate appointment. 10. Considering the aforesaid fact and also the fact which has now germinated with the passage of time that the fact remains that the death of the father of the petitioner has chanced as back as on 09.11.2002 and now sufficient period has lapsed, the very purpose of the compassionate appointment to meet the emergent need of the family stand exhausted, because sufficient time has lapsed and the family/dependents have been able to survives themselves, hence, this Court does not find any anomaly in the impugned order of rejection, consequently, the writ petition fails and is accordingly dismissed. 11. However, there would be no order as to costs. (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.) 27.02.2019 Mahinder/

title: SPA/1059/2018 of YOGESH KUMAR Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND THROUGH PRINCIPAL SECRETARY SCHOOL EDUCATION DEHRADUN
quotes: e learned counsel for the respondents and is, therefore, ordered. 2. This appeal is preferred against the order passed by the learned Single Judge in WPSS No. 2627 of 2015 dated 29.10.2018. The appellant herein sought a writ of certiorari to quash the orders dated 23.07.2013 and 28.05.2012 passed by the District Education Officer (Basic), Haridwar. 3. Facts, to the limited extent necessary, are that the appellant-writ petitioner was appointed on compassionate grounds, on 02.01.2004, as an Assistant Teacher (untrained scale), since he did not possess the requisite qualification to be appointed as an Assistant Teacher in the regular scale. The appellant-writ petitioner secured the stipulated education qualifications thereafter, and by proceedings dated 26.06.2006, his services were confirmed as an Assistant Teacher in a regular scale. A seniority list of Assistant Teachers was prepared by the Distri

llant-writ petitioner, as an Assistant Teacher, could not be reckoned from a date prior to when he fell in the cadre of Assistant Teacher; and, consequently, the respondents had rightly calculated the appellant-writ petitioner's seniority from 2006 instead of 2004. 5. Sri Ajay Veer Pundir, learned counsel for the appellant-writ petitioner, would submit that relaxation, in possessing the requisite qualification, is given to persons 3 appointed on compassionate grounds under the Dying-in-Harness Rules; since appointment is made to provide aid to the family in financial distress, a person who does not possess the requisite qualification is also considered for appointment; their appointment is conditional on their securing the prescribed qualifications within the specified period; the petitioner had secured the prescribed qualifications within the stipulated time; since his appointment as an Assistant
tail: qualifications within a specified period. The order of appointment, enclosed to the writ petition, does not also disclose that the appointment is conditional. It merely states that the petitioner was being appointed as an Assistant Teacher (untrained). The very fact that the appellant-writ petitioner was not appointed as an Assistant Teacher in a regular scale, but was appointed in the post of Assistant Teacher (untrained) is, by itself, proof that he was appointed as an Assistant Teacher (untrained) only because he did not possess the prescribed qualifications. Consequent on his securing the required qualifications, the appellant-writ petitioner was appointed as an Assistant Teacher in a regular scale in the year 2006; and his seniority has been rightly 4 reckoned as an Assistant Teacher only from that date, and not from 02.01.2004 when he was appointed as an Assistant Teacher (untrained). 7. Inference in an intra-Court appeal would be justified only if the order under appeal suffers from a patent illegality. We find no such infirmity in the order under appeal. The appeal fails and is, accordingly, dismissed. No costs. (N.S. Dhanik, J.) (Ramesh Ranganathan, C.J.) 27.03.2019 A.kaur

title: WPSS/3072/2018 of Soni Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS
quotes: eral for the State of Uttarakhand/respondent no. 1. Mr. Lalit Samant, Advocate for respondent nos. 2 to 4. In this writ petition the arguments started in the pre-lunch session and it continued thereafter in the post-lunch session. The facts involved in the writ petition are that the petition has been preferred by the petitioner now on 30.08.2018 against an order dated 26.03.2014 passed by respondent no. 4 after four years, whereby, his claim for compassionate appointment on account of the death of his father, who met with the sad demise on 02.06.2004, stood rejected by an order passed as back as on 2014. Challenging the said order, the petitioner has preferred the writ petition only on 30.08.2018 at a highly belated stage. A prayer after argument was made by the counsel for posting the matter after winter vacations, that prayer was declined by the Court because the argument has continued from the

ner that the Court has rather made up his mind to dismiss the writ petition. This is an experssion caused on the Court, which at least is not expected from the officer of the Court and it is highly deprecated by this Court. The Court is refraining from observing further and limiting itself to this observation only but, with a warning for future to the counsel for the petitioner. Even otherwise also it is a settled preposition that appointment on compassionate ground cannot be claimed as of his right, it is only a compassion, which is intended to be given to the bereaved family to tied away the immediate crisis, which has suddenly befallen on the family because of the loss of the bread winner of the family, it cannot be claimed as of right and at the whims of the dependant at their free will, there has to be a reasonable time within which the dependant is expected to approach to Court when there is
tail: easonable time within which the dependant is expected to approach to Court when there is denial by the authorities. In the present case it is not in dispute that the death of the father has taken place way back in 2004, wherein, after the petitioner had applied for a compassionate appointment on 15.06.2004, which stood rejected by an order dated 26.03.2014, the petitioner even after being made aware of the order of rejection sat over it and had not preferred a writ petition within a reasonable time and the writ petition had been preferred only after a lapse of four years on 30.08.2018, which is barred by laches. Even let us presume that laches may not be so significant for the purposes of entertaining the writ petition, but the issue, which is being agitated regarding an appointment on compassionate grounds, has lost its significance, since the family has survived since 02.06.2004 after the death of the bread winner, which is too long a period to now consider for grant of compassionate appointment in the light of the relief claimed for. Thus, this Court does not find any merit in the writ petition. Writ Petition is, accordingly, dismissed. (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.) 08.01.2019 Pooja

quotes: rsus State of Uttarakhand and others. ÖÖ Respondents. Present: Mr. C.K. Sharma, Advocate for the petitioner. Mr. V.D. Bisen, Brief Holder for the State of Uttarakhand / respondents. Honíble Alok Singh, J. 1. Petitionerís step mother namely late Ms. Prema Tiwari was serving as Assistant Teacher in Primary School, Reyuni, Majhkhali, Ranikhet, District Almora. She died during her service period. After the death of his mother, petitioner applied for compassionate appointment under the Dying in Harness Rules. Respondent Department rejected the claim of the petitioner inter alia on the ground that as per High School Certificate, petitionerís date of birth is 30.06.1977 while as per school record, Ms. Prema Tiwari, joined her duties on 01.07.1977 after summer vacation and she did not avail any maternity leave. Therefore, petitioner cannot be son of Ms. Prema Tiwari. Against the order of District Educatio

te by giving benefit of doubt in procuring the alleged appointment letter dated 24.08.2002 but this does not establish that the said appointment letter dated 24.08.2002 is genuine. District Education Officer has already denied its sanctity. When there is no appointment letter issued in favour of the petitioner, therefore, no relief, as sought in the writ petition, can be granted by this Court. 4. There is another aspect of the matter. In my view compassionate appointment is not a right but it is a concession. Honíble Apex Court in the case of Bhawani Prasad Sonkar Vs. Union of India and others reported in 2011 (4) SCC 209 has held as under: ì20. Thus, while considering a claim for employment on compassionate ground, the following factors have to be borne in mind: (i) Compassionate employment cannot be made in the absence of rules or regulations issued by the Government or a public authority. The r
tail: ment is granted to meet the sudden crisis on account of death of breadwinner while in service. While considering the claim for compassionate appointment, financial condition of family of deceased employee must be taken into consideration. The object to grant 4 compassionate appointment is to provide immediate help to the dependents of deceased employee, so that they may not die in starvation. 6. It is settled position of law that compassionate appointment is not a Rule and cannot be sought, as a matter of right. The compassionate appointment is a concession and exception to public appointment provided under Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution of India, therefore, to seek a concession of compassionate appointment, claimant must prove his financial condition and must prove that in the event of non grant of compassionate appointment, claimant would face financial crisis and may die in starvation. 7. In the present case, petitioner applied for compassionate appointment in 1998 and now, it is 2018, therefore, this Court cannot issue direction for compassionate appointment. 8. In view of the above discussion, writ petition fails and is hereby dismissed. (Alok Singh, J.) 04.10.2018 SKS

reported in 2011 (4) SCC 209 has held as under: ì20. Thus, while considering a claim for employment on compassionate ground, the following factors have to be borne in mind: (i) Compassionate employment cannot be made in the absence of rules or regulations issued by the Government or a public authority. The 2 request is to be considered strictly in accordance with the governing scheme, and no discretion as such is left with any authority to make compassionate appointment dehors the scheme. (ii) An application for compassionate employment must be preferred without undue delay and has to be considered within a reasonable period of time. (iii) An appointment on compassionate ground is to meet the sudden crisis occurring in the family on account of the death or medical invalidation of the bread winner while in service. Therefore, compassionate employment cannot be granted as a matter of course by way
tail: s settled position of law that compassionate appointment is not a Rule and cannot be sought, as a matter of right. The compassionate appointment is a concession and exception to public appointment provided under Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution of India, therefore, to seek a concession of compassionate appointment, claimant must prove his financial condition and must prove that in the event of non grant of compassionate appointment, claimant would face financial crisis and may die in starvation. 6. Since application seeking compassionate appointment was moved in the year 2012 and present petition is filed in the year 2017 and now, in the year 2018, when petitioner would have crossed the upper age limit to seek public appointment, writ of Mandamus commanding the respondents to provide compassionate appointment to the petitioner seems to be unjustified, at this stage. Therefore, prayer no. 1 cannot be granted. The case of the petitioner was turned down on 06.05.2005 on the ground that the family has been paid terminal benefits of Rs.4.18 Lakh and the family pension was being paid @ Rs.3,043/-. Learned counsel for the respondent nos.2 and 5 has drawn the attention of this Court towards the letter dated 01.01.1998, dealing with compassionate appointment. According to Para "L", the condition of the family has to be seen while considering the ca

asis including gratuity amount recovered, employee's/ employer's contribution to provident fund, any compensation paid by the Bank or its Welfare Fund, income of family from other sources, income of other family members from employment, or otherwise the size of the family and liabilities, if any. In the instant case, the family has been paid a meagre sum of Rs.4.18 Lakh as terminal benefits. The family pension is also paltry. No person can claim compassionate appointment as a matter of right but definitely has a right to be considered for appointment in accordance with law and the parameters prescribed. The petitioner has been denied for appointment on compassionate basis on the ground that the family was not living in penury and the funds were sufficient for living. This issue raised in writ petition is no more res integra in view of judgment rendered by their Lordships of Hon'ble Supreme Court i
tail: sum of Rs.4.18 lakh. A sum of Rs.4.18 lakh as terminal benefits cannot be held sufficient to make both ends meet. The underlying principle to offer compassionate appointment is to enable the family to tide over the financial crises faced by the family after the death of the sole bread earner. Learned Counsel appearing on behalf of respondent nos.2 and 5 has relied upon the judgment rendered by their Lordships of Hon'ble Supreme Court in (2004) 7 SCC 271 in the case of "General Manager (D& B) and others vs. Kunti Tiwary and another." The ratio of the judgment is also that the family, who was living in penurious circumstances alone, is entitled to compassionate appointment. It is evident as discussed hereinabove that the petitioner's family has got meager pensionary/retiral benefits. Accordingly, the writ petition is allowed. The petitioner lost her husband on 20.08.2004. Petitioner's husband was working as class IV employee in the office of District Judge, Almora. Petitioner submitted an application seeking compassionate appointment on class-IV post. The case of the petitioner was rejected vide order dated 15.09.2004 by the District Judge by holding that the petitioner was not in possession of minimum educational qualification and she was overage. The District Judge has rejected the case of the petitioner mechanically without due application of mind. The petitioner' husband was working as class-IV employee. She has sought the appointment on compassionate basi
tail: olding that the petitioner was not in possession of minimum educational qualification and she was overage. The District Judge has rejected the case of the petitioner mechanically without due application of mind. The petitioner' husband was working as class-IV employee. She has sought the appointment on compassionate basis only as a class-IV employee. In view of this, the District Judge, Almora should have considered the case of the petitioner by relaxing the norms. The purpose of making compassionate appointment is to permit the family to tide over the crises faced immediately after the death of bread earner. The petitioner has to support herself and her children. Even if the petitioner was overage, her case was required to be considered sympathetically for the simple reason that even if she was appointed at the age of 47 years, she was entitled to pension after putting in 10 years of service. Accordingly, the writ petition is allowed. Impugned order passed by the District Judge is quashed and set aside. The District Judge, Almora is directed to reconsider the case of the petitioner sympathetically in view of the observations made herein above. (Rajiv Sharma, J.) 25.04.2018 Kaushal

Mr. Arvind Vashisth, Senior Advocate with Ms. Monika Pant, Advocate for the respondent Nos.2 to 5. The petitionerís father was working as Daftari. He died on 16.09.2000. The petitioner submitted an application for appointment on compassionate basis on 14.02.2001. It was rejected on 19.03.2003. The petitioner filed a WPSS No.361 of 2005. It was decided on 03.03.2006 whereby the respondent-Bank was directed to reconsider the case of the petitioner. The respondent-Bank again rejected the case of the petitioner on 17.10.2006 on the ground that the family was not living in penury. The petitioner was getting meager pension of Rs.6269 as on 17.10.2006. She got only partial sum of Rs.3,47

etitioner on 17.10.2006 on the ground that the family was not living in penury. The petitioner was getting meager pension of Rs.6269 as on 17.10.2006. She got only partial sum of Rs.3,47,000/- towards retiral benefits. No person can claim compassionate appointment as a matter of right but definitely has a right to be considered for appointment in accordance with law and the parameters prescribed. The petitioner has been denied for appointment on compassionate basis on the ground that the family was not living in penury and the funds were sufficient for living. This issue raised in writ petition is no more res integra in view of judgment rendered by their Lordships of Honíble Supreme Court in (2000) 6 SCC 493 in the case of Balbir Kaur & another Vs. Steel Authoirty of India & others. Their Lordships have held has under :- "But in our view this Fam ily Benefit Schem e cannot in any way be equated wi
tail: me amount towards retiral benefits a sum of Rs.3.47 lakhs. A sum of Rs.3.47 lakhs as retiral benefits cannot be held sufficient to make both ends meet. The underlying principle to offer compassionate appointment is to enable the family to tide over the financial crises faced by the family after the death of the sole bread earner. Learned Senior Counsel appearing on behalf of Bank/respondent Nos.2 to 5 has relied upon the judgment rendered by their Lordships of Honíble Supreme Court in (2004) 7 SCC 271 in the case of General Manager (D& B) and others vs. Kunti Tiwary and another. The ratio of the judgment is also that the family, who was living in penurious circumstances alone, is entitled to compassionate appointment. It is evident as discussed hereinabove that the petitionerís family has got meager pensionary/retiral benefits. The writ petition is allowed. Impugned order dated 17.10.2006 is quashed and set aside. The respondents are directed to decide the case of the petitioner for appointment on compassionate basis without insisting on an income ceiling, within a period of six weeks from today. Pending application, stands disposed of accordingly. (Rajiv Sharma, J.) 07.03.2018 JKJ

It is evident from Rule 5(1) that the State Governmet shall, on making an application for the purpose, can be given a suitable employment in government service on a post except the post which is within the purview of the Uttar Pradesh Public Service Commission, in relaxation of the normal recruitment rules if such person fulfils the educational

pay-scale of Rs.5200-20200/-, his appointment to the post of Clerk cannot be considered. There is fallacy in the decision dated 06.07.2015. title: AO/355/2015 of New India Assurance Co. Ltd. Vs Smt Janki Devi AND OTHERS
quotes: 013 was instituted by his wife Smt. Janki Devi which has culminated into granting of compensation, as indicated above. Learned Counsel for the appellant insurance company has agitated the quantum of the award on the ground that the deceased Girish Chandra Pandey was a gardener in Almora Jal Sansthan and his total salary in the 2 month of November 2011, after deductions, was Rs. 13,257/-. His wife certainly must have got the appointment under the dying in harness rules, apart from other benefits like group insurance, gratuity, etc. Besides, since she was the alone dependent, hence the Tribunal has committed error by deducting only 1/3rd from the total amount of compensation towards the personal expenses of the deceased. I think the similar controversy was dealt with by this Court in AO No. 383/2011, New India Assurance Co. Ltd. v. Smt. Shakun Chitra & Others, decided on 22.7.2016, wherein this Court has

roversy in an another case Ramprasad Balmiki v. Anil Kumar Jain & Others, reported in 2008 (4) T.A.C. 385, the Hon. Apex Court has held that even the amount of pension would have mitigated the quantum of damages and same was required to be taken into consideration. In the present case as well, the deceased was a gardener in the government organisation. Hence in all probabilities, his sole dependant, the wife, should have got 3 the appointment on compassionate ground and the same has not been denied on the record. It can be assumed that this claimant widow must have been getting the pension, besides the job. Other benefits like gratuity, insurance, etc. would also be on the score while evaluating such compensation because it has been said time and again in the many judgments of the Hon. Apex Courts and the various High Courts that death of the earning member of a family can never be taken as a wind
tail: ny judgments of the Hon. Apex Courts and the various High Courts that death of the earning member of a family can never be taken as a windfall for other members of the family and the amount so evaluated should not be taken as largesse in such matters. The whole object behind this social legislation is to save the dependants from indigence or from being on the road in the absence of bread earner. This widow, the sole dependant of the deceased Girish Chandra Pandey, is further in the privileged position that she is alone in receiving all the benefits on account of death of her husband. Visualising that she must have got enough, I struck down the whole quantum as awarded by the Tribunal and reduce it to rupees five lakhs only as a lump sum compensation, which has already been deposited by the appellant insurance company and the same shall be released to her as and when applied for. Registry shall remit the amount of compulsory statutory deposit along with the interest accrued on it to the Tribunal concerned. Impugned judgment and order is modified to the extent indicated above and the appeal stands allowed in aforesaid terms. Let the LCR be sent back. (Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.) Prabodh

title: WPSS/691/2016 of Nisha Lohani Vs State Of Uttarakhand AND OTHERS
quotes: te for the petitioner. Mr. B.P.S. Mer, Brief Holder for the State. Reserved on:30.03.2017 Delivered on:24.04.2017 Hon'ble Rajiv Sharma , J. 1. The father of the petitioner died in harness on 26.06.2013. He was working as peon in Girls Government Higher Secondary School, Tallital, Nainital. The mother of the petitioner submitted a representation on 28.07.2014 before the competent authority to consider the name of the petitioner for appointment on compassionate ground but no decision had been taken by the respondents. Petitioner approached this Court by way of filing of WPSS No.2331 of 2015 which was disposed of with a direction to the respondents to take a decision on the representation as expeditiously as possible. The representation was rejected vide order dated 15.01.2016 primarily on the ground that 'married daughter' does not fall within the ambit of "Family" as per the Rule 2(c) of the U.P. R

ambit of "Family" as per the Rule 2(c) of the U.P. Recruitment of Dependants of Government Servants Dying in Harness Rules, 1974 (hereinafter referred to as "The Dying in Harness Rules,1974") adopted by State of Uttarakhand. 2. Ms. Mamta Joshi, Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner has vehemently argued that the 2 Rule 2(c) of the Dying and Harness Rules is arbitrary and unreasonable, since, it excludes the married daughter for getting compassionate appointment after the death of her father. The Dying and Harness Rules is also violative of Articles 14, 15 & 16 of the Constitution of India, since the married son is not excluded but only married daughter is excluded from getting the job on the compassionate ground. 3. Learned State counsel appearing for respondents has supported the Dying and Harness Rules. 4. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the documents available
tail: n Harness Rules, 1974 is violative of Articles 14, 15 & 16 of the Constitution of India. It also creates artificial classification between married son and married daughter only on the basis of sex. Since married son is included in the definition of the "family", there is no reason why the married daughter should not be included in the definition of "family". It is a case of gender discrimination 14. Son and daughter are supposed to take care of the parents at the old age. The married son is to be treated at par with the unmarried daughter. Not considering the married daughter for compassionate appointment merely on the basis of marriage is patently arbitrary and unreasonable. 15. Accordingly, the writ petition is allowed. The exclusion of married daughter from the ambit of the expression "family" under Rule 2(c) of the U.P. Recruitment of Dependants of Government Servants Dying in Harness Rules, 1974 is declared illegal and unconstitutional, being violative of Articles 14,15 & 16 of the Constitution of India and respondents are directed to consider the claim of the petitioner for compassionate appointment, within a period of eight weeks from today. (Rajiv Sharma, J.) JKJ 24.04.2017

quotes: WPSS No.2229 of 2014 Honíble Rajiv Sharma, J. Mr. K.P. Upadhyay, Advocate for the petitioner. Mr. B.P.S. Mer, Brief Holder for the State. Petitioner was appointed under dying in harness Rules in the Public Works Department on 04.08.2000. He was appointed against substantive vacancy. More vacancies were also lying vacant at the time of his appointment of compassionate ground. However, the fact of the matter is that petitioner was treated as surplus employee on 17.10.2001. Petitioner has approached this Court seeking seniority. Thereafter, State Government has framed the rules called as ìUttarakhand Government Employees Absorptio

artment without any break since 13.12.2001. Petitioner was under genuine apprehension that he would be absorbed as per the Rules, 2011 w.e.f. 04.08.2000 and not from 13.12.2001 when he was transferred in Commercial Tax Department. He approached this Court seeking absorption from back date by way of filing WPSS No.321 of 2012 which was decided on 03.09.2014. Paragraph 3 of the judgment reads as under :- ì3.Normally, appointments which are made on compassionate ground under the Dying in Harness Rules are substantive appointments, but in the present case, it appears that the frequent transfer of the petitioner from one Department to another suggests that the appointment itself was done after creation of a supernumerary post. Moreover, such transfers are only being made in the case of surplus posts. The fact, however, remains that the petitioner stood transferred to the Commercial Tax Department on 13
tail: cial Tax Department. He was not required to be considered as surplus employee since he was appointed against substantive vacancy. This Court has considered that there was nothing in the Rules, 2011 which debars the concerned authority to absorb the petitioner from retrospective effect or from the date when he was actually transferred to the Commercial Tax Department. This Court in these circumstances had issued a direction to the respondents to consider the case of petitioner for absorption from retrospective effect but only after calling objections from all the employees in the cadre, as they might have been genuine grievance in the absorption of the petitioner. The decision dated 14.11.2014 is in contravention of the judgment dated 03.09.2014. Petitionerís case for absorption was required to be considered from the date when he came in the Commercial Tax Department i.e. 13.12.2001 as per Rules, 2011. Accordingly, the writ petition is allowed. Annexure No.1 dated 14.11.2014 is hereby quashed and set aside. Respondents are directed to absorb the petitioner w.e.f. 13.12.2001 with all consequential benefits, within a period of 10 weeks from today. [[[ (Rajiv Sharma, J.) JKJ 17.04.2017

Reserved on:27.03.2017 Delivered on:06.04.2017 Hon'ble Rajiv Sharma , J. 1. The father of the petitioner died in harness on 23.02.2014. He was the employee of Udham Singh Nagar District Co-operative Bank Limited. Petitioner submitted an application seeking appointment on compassionate grounds. The application was rejected vide order dated 02.05.2016 primarily on the ground that 'married daughter' is not included in the definition of the "family". The compassionate appointment is regulated by U.P. Co-operative Committee Employees Service Regulations, 1975. In a note appended to the expression "Family", the married daughter is not included. 2. Mr. Pankaj Miglani has vehemently argued that the note appended to regulation i.e.

ommittee Employees Service Regulations, 1975 is arbitrary and unreasonable, since, it excludes the married daughter for getting compassionate appointment after the death of her father. The note given under the U.P. Co-operative Committee Employees Service Regulations, 1975 is also violative of Articles 14, 15 & 16 of the Constitution of India, since the married son is not excluded but only married daughter is excluded from getting the job on the compassionate grounds. 3. Learned counsel appearing for respondents has supported the U.P. Co-operative Committee Employees Service Regulations, 1975. 4. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the documents available on record carefully. 5. Petitioner lost her father on 23.02.2014. It is not in dispute that the case of the petitioner was rejected on 02.05.2016 on the ground that married daughter is not included in the definition of the "f
tail: ice Regulations, 1975 is violative of Articles 14, 15 & 16 of the Constitution of India. It also creates an artificial classification between married son and married daughter only on the basis of sex. Since married son is included in the definition of the "family", there is no reason why the married daughter should not be included in the definition of "family". It is a case of gender discrimination 14. Son and daughter are supposed to take care of the parents at the old age. The married son is to be treated at par with the unmarried daughter. Not considering the married daughter for compassionate appointment merely on the basis of marriage is patently arbitrary and unreasonable. 15. Accordingly, the writ petition is allowed. In the year 2008 the petitioner moved an application before the authoritiesí concerned seeking appointment on compassionate ground under the Recruitment of Dependent of Government Servant Dying in Harness Rules, 1974. 2. Appointments in public service are made, subject to reservations, etc., purely on the basis of merit. There is a selection process involved in such matters and only if one qualifies the selection process, one is liable to be given an appointment. Appointment given on compassionate ground under the Dying in Harness rules is an exception to the rule

d above. Such an exception has been carved out by the Legislature in a welfare State so that a family who has been deprived of its only earning member is able to meet the immediate hardship, which has befallen upon the family due to death of its only bread-winner. In most cases, such families who have lost their bread-winner are at the stage of penury and face extreme financial hardship. The provision of law referred above 2 (i.e. appointment on compassionate ground) thus seeks to mitigate the hardship of a family in distress. 3. In this matter, the petitioner has admittedly applied for appointment after a period of more than 21 years. Such an application cannot be considered not only because it is highly belated but also on the ground that petitioner has preferred the present writ petition itself in the year 2015. 4. In view of the above, no relief can be granted to the petitioner. Writ petition

title: AO/142/2012 of SURESH DHIMAN and OTHERS Vs NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED
quotes: is not a gospel truth even on the basis of Sarla Verma Case and it can be varied by the Court considering all around circumstances of the particular case and family but on this score, I would not like to lessen it any further than thirteen (13). Learned counsel has relied upon an of-late law laid down by the Honíble Apex Court in the case of Vimal Kanwar and others Vs. Kishore Dan and others, 2013 (7) SCC 476, wherein, it has been held that the compassionate appointment can be one of the conditions of service of an employee, and if a scheme to that effect has been framed by the employer, then this factor cannot stated to be an advantage receivable by the heirs on account of oneís death and it does not have any co-relation with the amount receivable in a statute occasioned on account of accidental death. 4 It was further held that a ìpecuniary advantageî, which comes under the periphery of Motor V

se cases were never referred to by either of the party to the Honíble Apex Court while adjudicating Vimal Kanwar case. It has been a settled proposition of law, which is holding reigns even now that the death in the accident can never be taken as a windfall to the rest of the family members. The compensation, which has awarded by the Tribunals, is not a largesse. This beneficial legislation has been enacted by the Parliament in order to save the dependants of the deceased from indigence. The calculation of compensation can never be 5 evaluated in a mechanical manner; it all depends on several factors and varies from facts to facts of the different cases. In the case, in hand, it is difficult to remain in oblivion that Shri Suresh Dhiman himself was gainfully employed inasmuch as he was Head Constable, posted in Rudraprayag Police Station, so, the children of the wedded couple were not depended solely on the incom
tail: e personal expenses, as argued by learned counsel for the dependants, is the far cry and it should have been one-half, instead of one-third as has been done by the Tribunal. Deducting one-half, the amount comes to Rs.1,54,992/-. I apply the multiplier of ì13î, as discussed above, which comes to Rs.20,14,896/-. This Court is not inclined to disturb the findings of learned Tribunal on other scores. In view of what has been set forth above, AO No.58 of 2012, filed by the Insurance Company is hereby allowed modifying the award to the extent, as indicated above, and at the same time, I dismiss the AO No.142 of 2012, filed by the claimants. Insurance company is directed to satisfy the award as modified by this Court within a period of six weeks from today. After such deposit is made, the Tribunal is directed to release the entire amount in favour of the claimants as per their respective shares. title: WPSS/359/2012 of SMT BIMLA DEVI Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND and OTHERS
quotes: UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL Writ Petition (S/S) No. 359 of 2012 Smt. Bimla Devi ÖPetitioner Vs State of Uttarakhand and others ÖRespondent Mr. C.D. Bahuguna, Senior Advocate, assisted by Mr. A.K. Verma, Advocate, present for the petitioner. Mr. N.P. Sah, learned Standing Counsel present for the State/respondents. Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J 1. The petitioner before this Court claims appointment on regular post of Beldar in Public Works Department on compassionate grounds, as her husband who was a Beldar, according to the petitioner died while in harness on 09.07.2005. 2. In the first round of litigation, for the same relief, the writ petition of the petitioner was disposed of with a direction to the concerned authority to consider the appointment of the petitioner on a regular vacancy. The same has now been considered and has been rejected by the authority concerned. The reasons assigned in the impugn

earned Single Judge of this Court was set aside. In short, therefore the order of regularization which stood in favour of the petitionerís husband and other similarly situated employees was set aside by the Division Bench of this Court. Hence, in a fact, is that the husband of the petitioner was never regularized in service. Meanwhile, on 09.07.2005 the husband of the petitioner passed away. The petitioner moved an application for appointment on compassionate grounds, which was not considered, and as already referred above, she was constrained to file writ petition before this Court, which was disposed of by this Court vide judgment and order dated 18.10.2011. 4. Now, vide impugned order dated 07.01.2012 the respondents have categorically stated that since the husband of the petitioner was not a regular employee therefore the petitioner is not entitled for regular selection on compassionate ground
tail: though regularly appointed nor was he continuing in a regular vacancy, as contemplated in the above provision. Hence, he was only a work charge employee. A work charge employee by its very nomenclature is not in the regular establishment, is not working on any sanctioned post, and therefore the death of such an employee would not mean that the dependents or family members would be entitled for appointment on compassionate grounds. The claim of the petitioner cannot be sustained and it has been rightly rejected. 6. Having made the above determination, however, this Court is also conscious of the fact that the petitioner was initially appointed as a daily rated worker in the department itself after the death of her husband in the year 2005 and by now as the learned Counsel himself submits she is working in the work charge establishment. The writ petition stands disposed with a direction that on considerations of the past services of the petitioner, the candidature of the petitioner be considered for regular absorption in accordance with law as and when such a vacancy arises. Her vis-a-vis other employees should also be taken into consideration. (Sudhanshu Dhulia, J.) 08.03.2016 Rahul

title: SPA/603/2014 of Vipin Kumar Vs Managing Director Uttarakhand Transport Corp AND OTHERS
quotes: r. He approached this Court seeking the following prayers: "(i) Issue writ rule or direction in the nature of certiorari quashing the impugned order dated 29.04.2010 passed by the Managing Director Respondent no. 1 and 18-12-04 passed by the respondent no.3/Regional Manager Uttarakhand Road Transport Corporation. (ii) Issue writ rule or direction in the nature of mandamus commanding the respondents to the consider the claim for appointment under dying in harness of the petitioner and appoint him on the compassionate ground." 2. Learned Single Judge dismissed the writ petition. Learned Single Judge noted the facts as follows: Mother of the appellant was a Class IV employee with the respondent Corporation. She died in the year 1997. Appellant applied in 2001, when he was only 10 years' old and he could not be appointed. Since 2004, appellant has been making regular representations to the Authorities, but

ot be appointed. Since 2004, appellant has been making regular representations to the Authorities, but in vain. Appellant had filed Writ Petition No. 81 of 2010 (S/S), which was disposed of by directing the Authorities to decide the Application of the appellant for appointment on compassionate grounds within three months, which is rejected on 29th April, 2010 by a speaking order on the ground primarily that the basic purpose of appointment under Dying in Harness Rules is that the family of the person, who has died in Harness should be able to meet the hardships, which have arisen due to death of the breadwinner of the family and these hardships have to be looked into immediately. With the passage of time, the same hardship, as it existed at the time of the death of incumbent, who died in harness, cannot be said to remain. Thirteen years have gone by. Therefore, the order dated 29th April, 2010 has right
tail: rder dated 29th April, 2010 has rightly been passed. It is also found by the learned Single Judge that the family of the appellant consists only of the appellant. On this ground, the Court was not inclined to interfere in the matter. 3. We heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned counsel for the respondents. 4. We are not persuaded to take a different view having regard to the purport of the Dying in Harness. Learned counsel for the appellant, however, would submit that the appellant was engaged on contractual basis through an outsourcing Agency and he prays that the appellant may be regularized. Learned counsel for the appellant has also a case that the finding regarding family is not correct as the appellant has a brother. Learned counsel for the respondents would submit that the claim made is not for regularization, but is for appointment on compassionate ground. While affirming the judgment of the learned Single Judge, we only make it clear that this order will not stand in the way of the appellant pursuing his claim for regularisation as per the Rules. 5. The Appeal is, accordingly, dismissed. (V.K. Bist, J.) (K.M. Joseph, C.J.) 09.09.2015 09.09.2015 Rathour

quotes: , Advocate for the petitioners. Mr. S.K. Jain, Senior Advocate assisted by Mr. Siddhartha Jain, Advocate for the respondents. Honíble Alok Singh, J. (Oral) Present petition is filed seeking writ of mandamus commanding the respondent-Bank to release Rs. 6,00,000/- in favour of the petitioner towards the financial relief on account of death of his mother on 10.03.1997 and commanding the respondents to consider the candidature of the petitioner for compassionate appointment under the Dying in Harness Rules. Undisputedly, Manoj Kumar, father of the petitioner was working as part-time sweeper in Khatima Branch of the respondent-Bank; Manoj Kumar, father of the petitioner had expired on 22.07.1993; therefore, Smt. Gauri Devi, widow of Manoj Kumar and mother of the present petitioner was given appointment as sweeper under the Dying in Harness Rules; unfortunately, Gauri Devi also expired 10.03.1997, leav

Km. Sonam aged about 7 years as well as Norati Devi, grand-mother of the petitioner; Smt. Norati Devi, grand-mother of the petitioner made representation to the respondent-Bank for grant of terminal dues so that she may take care of minor children whereupon all the dues and gratuity was paid to Smt. Norati Devi on 01.06.2006; having received the gratuity, present petitioner preferred Writ Petition No. 467 of 2005(S/S) before this Court 2 seeking compassionate appointment which was finally disposed of vide judgment dated 03.03.2006 directing the Bank to take decision on the representation of the petitioner considering the financial status of the petitioner; in compliance of the judgment dated 03.03.2006, General Manager of the Bank has decided to pay ex-gratia financial relief of Rs. 3,00,000/- towards full and final settlement to the petitioner and Smt. Norati Devi, grand mother of the petitioner
tail: of the judgment dated 03.03.2006, General Manager of the Bank has decided to pay ex-gratia financial relief of Rs. 3,00,000/- towards full and final settlement to the petitioner and Smt. Norati Devi, grand mother of the petitioner on behalf of other two children; in compliance of the decision on the representation dated 27.05.2006; payment of Rs. 3,00,000/- was received by the petitioner, his brother, sister and grand-mother. Thereafter, present petition was again filed seeking financial help as well as the compassionate appointment under the Dying in Harness Rules. Since, in the earlier writ petition compassionate appointment was sought wherein direction was issued to take the decision on the representation of the petitioner and in compliance of the direction issued by this Court, petitioner and others were paid ex-gratia amount to the tune of Rs. 3,00,000/- over and above the terminal dues and gratuity, therefore, second writ petition seeking compassionate appointment and enhanced ex-gratia financial relief is not maintainable. tail: , who was a Class-IV employee in revenue department of Tehsil Dhari, District Nainital, died during his service tenure. So, in his place, his son Tara Chand got employment under the Dying-in-Harness Rules, but unfortunately, Tara Chand also died on 15.05.1996. After his death, this petition was filed on 04.02.2015 by the married sister Smt. Pushpa Devi, who is aged about 32 years, seeking employment under the Dying-in-Harness Rules. Her claim has been supported by her mother Smt. Savitri Devi. Learned State Counsel has taken this Court to the concerned Rules of 1974, wherein it has been envisaged that such employment can only be granted to either (i) Wife or Husband of the deceased, (ii) Sons (iii) Unmarried and widowed daughters, (iv) if the deceased was unmarried Government Servant, then his brother, unmarried sister and widowed mother, dependant on the deceased Government Servant. Having regard to the above provision, the Court finds that the petitioner does not fall under any of the categories as mentioned in the Rules. She is a married lady having a surviving husband. So, the petition is bereft of merit and it is dismissed accordingly. (Servesh Kumar Gupta, J.) 29.06.2015 Ravi

Having heard learned counsel for the parties, it transpires that petitionerís services were hired by the Department as a daily-wager and he is working as such since December, 1998. As per the version of petitioner, his father, who was also a daily wager in the Department, died on 11.2.1999 and in place of his father, he was inducted in service on the basis of dying-in-harness (yet no appointment letter to this effect has been brought on record by the petitioner). However, for some reasons, he was removed from the service on 12.5.2008 but by the order of this Court, his engagement for work, which he was already performing, continued in the Department. In the instant petition, petitioner seeks for issuance of writ of mandamus for his regular appointment on the basis of dying-in-harness rules. The Honíble Apex Court in
tail: eady performing, continued in the Department. In the instant petition, petitioner seeks for issuance of writ of mandamus for his regular appointment on the basis of dying-in-harness rules. The Honíble Apex Court in the cases of ëState of Haryana vs. Surendra Kumarí 1997 (76) FLR Page 305 and ëState of Haryana vs. Jasmer Singh & othersí 1977 (75) FLR Page 776, has held that the daily wage employees do not hold any post. Thus, these employees cannot be equated 2 with regular work for the purposes of their wages. Thereafter, in a number of cases, the similar view was adopted by the Apex Court. So, this petition is devoid of any merit and is hereby dismissed. However, it is made clear that if there is a vacancy and the scope of work is persisting on the post whereon the petitioner is working, then, subject to his loyalty and dedication towards work, he may be permitted to continue to work as a daily wager till the posts are filled up by issuing the advertisement calling application forms from the eligible candidates. title: WPSS/683/2012 of MOHD USMAN KHAN Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND and OTHERS
quotes: older, present for the State/respondents. Honíble Sudhanshu Dhulia, J. (Oral) 1. The father of the petitioner who was a regular employee in the Agricultural Department in the State of Uttarakhand died while in harness on 26.12.2010, leaving behind his wife, two daughters and two sons including one who is already gainfully employed with the Forest Department of Government of Uttarakhand. The present petitioner, however, applied for appointment on compassionate ground on 2nd February, 2011. This application has been rejected on 27.08.2011 on the ground that one of the sons of the deceased employee is already in employment of Government i.e. in Uttarakhand Forest Department, therefore, appointment on compassionate ground cannot be given to the petitioner and, therefore, this reasoning adopted is totally wrong. 2. In the counter affidavit filed by respondent nos. 2, 3 and 4, they have relied upon Rule

that the person appointed under sub-rule (1) shall upkeep those other family members of the deceased Government Servant who are incapable for their own maintenance and were dependent of the abovesaid deceased Government servant immediately before his death.î 3. Now the contention of the State is that since elder brother of the petitioner, namely, Sri Noman Khan is a Government employee, therefore, the petitioner cannot be granted appointment on compassionate ground under Dying in Harness Rules. This argument of the State Counsel is totally misconceived, inasmuch, as Rule 5 only 3 states that such an appointment shall not be given in case the spouse of the deceased is already employed in the Government service. It is not the case, where the spouse of the deceased was employed in Government service. One who is employed in the Government service is the son of the deceased, who is presently living se
tail: t shall not be given in case the spouse of the deceased is already employed in the Government service. It is not the case, where the spouse of the deceased was employed in Government service. One who is employed in the Government service is the son of the deceased, who is presently living separately and merely because one of the sons of the deceased is employed, it cannot be a ground of denying the employment to the petitioner. Moreover, what further goes in favour of the petitioner is that the elder son of the deceased is living separately and is not supporting the family (the one who is employed), as such, the son of the deceased should be given an appointment on compassionate ground under Dying in Harness Rules and the appointment of the petitioner. 4. In view thereof, the writ petition is allowed. The impugned order dated 27.08.2011, passed by the respondent no. 3 is quashed. title: SPA/271/2014 of Deepak Kumar Sahu Vs Union Of India AND OTHERS
quotes: unsel present for the respondents. Hon'ble V. K. Bist, A.C.J. (Oral) 1. Present Special Appeal has been filed by the appellant challenging the judgment dated 30.05.2014 passed by learned Single Judge in Writ Petition no.718 of 2014 (S/S), whereby the writ petition was dismissed on the ground of laches. The father of the petitioner-appellant died in harness on 02.07.1997. Thereafter, the petitioner's mother moved an application for appointment on compassionate ground under Dying-in-Harness Rules, in the year 1998. The said application for compassionate appointment was rejected, vide order dated 27.7.2002 wherein it was observed that the need for immediate assistance by way of compassionate appointment to tide over the emergency and crisis was lacking, as the petitioner's father died on 02.07.1997, i.e., 5 years ago from the date of rejection order. The application of the petitioner's mother was rej

on 02.07.1997, i.e., 5 years ago from the date of rejection order. The application of the petitioner's mother was rejected due to non-availability of sufficient vacancy within 5% quota. 2. It appears that after this rejection order, the mother of the petitioner did not challenge the same and kept silent for a considerable long period and only when the petitioner attained the age of majority in 2011, he (i.e. appellant) moved application -2- for compassionate appointment and when nothing was done by the respondent-department, a writ petition bearing no.718/2014 (S/S) was filed in the year 2014, wherein learned Single Judge, having considered the submissions of the petitioner's counsel came to the conclusion that it was too late on the day to consider such application in the year 2011, in as much as, the deceased employee died in the year 1997, his spouse applied for compassionate appointment in 19
tail: se, the family of the deceased employee seeking compassionate appointment had applied within a reasonable time and if the application seeking compassionate appointment is made in time, in that event, the pendency of such application will not come on the way of the family of the deceased seeking compassionate appointment. 5. In Manoj Kumar Saxena's case (supra), at the time of death of his (Manoj Kumar Sexena's) father in 1987, he was minor and when he attained the age of majority in 1993, applied for appointment on compassionate ground. The said pronouncement is not applicable to the facts of the present case, in as much as, in the instant case, the father of the petitioner died in 1997; the application moved by the petitioner's mother was rejected in 2002; the petitioner filed writ petition in 2014 seeking compassionate appointment; and once the application of the family of the deceased employee seeking appointment on compassionate ground is rejected, another family member of the said deceased is not entitled to move another application. 6. In view of above, the special appeal fails and is, accordingly, dismissed. (U. C. Dhyani, J.) (V. K. Bist, A.C.J.) Dated 16th July, 2014 Rawat

quotes: THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL Special Appeal No. 226 of 2010 Managing Director, Kumaon Mandal Vikas Nigam and another ........... Appellants Versus Manoj Singh Rautela ........... Respondent Present: Mr. Sandeep Kothari, Advocate for the appellants. Mr. S.S. Chaudhary, Advocate for the respondent. Coram: Hon'ble Barin Ghosh, C.J. Hon'ble V.K. Bist, J. BARIN GHOSH, C.J. (Oral) The U.P. Recruitment of Dependants of Government Servants Dying in Harness Rules, 1974 defines, amongst others, "Government Servant". It has been provided in Rule 2(a) (iii) of the said Rules that "Government Servant" means a Government Servant employed in connection with the affairs of Uttar Pradesh who though not regularly appointed, had put in three years' continuous service in regular vacancy in such employment. Taking into account such definition, several Division Benches of the Hon'ble Allahabad High Court held t

matter stands crystallized. 2. In the instant case, the father of the respondent/writ petitioner was a daily wage employee. The father of the respondent/writ petitioner died before reaching the ordinary age of superannuation prescribed for the Government servants. Respondent /writ petitioner contended that since his father being such a daily wage employee, was a Government servant covered by Rule 2(a)(iii) of the said Rules, he is entitled to a compassionate appointment. In the counter affidavit, it was contended that a daily wage employee is not a Government servant and after death of the father of the respondent/writ petitioner compassion was shown to the respondent/writ petitioner by giving him a daily wage employment. A learned Judge, who dealt with the writ petition, felt that the father of the respondent/writ petitioner was covered by Rule 2(a)(iii) of the said Rules and, accordingly, compa
tail: judgment and order under appeal, there was a confusion as to who were Government Servants within the meaning of definition of "Government Servant" given in Rule 2(a)(iii) of the said Rules and the learned Judge did nothing wrong in following the judgment, rendered in the case of Ravi Karan Singh, referred to above. However, having regard to the fact that the law has been explained by a Full Bench to the effect that daily wage employees are no employees either permanent, or 3 temporary, inasmuch as, their employment is for a day and, accordingly, commences in the morning and comes to end in the evening, there is no scope of such a person to render continuous service for three years. There is need to correct the judgment under appeal and since we have not been persuaded to take a different view then what has been taken by a Full Bench of the Hon'ble Allahabad High Court, we allow the appeal, set aside the judgment under appeal and dismiss the writ petition with a request to the appellants to continue the daily wage employment which they have accorded to the respondent/ writ petitioner till such engagement is required. (V.K. Bist, J.) (Barin Ghosh, C.J.) 30.04.2014 30.04.2014 P. Singh

Raj Pal Singh, father of the petitioner, expired on 14.12.1976 in harness. Petitioner, after attaining the age of majority, moved an application seeking compassionate appointment on 19.02.1996, however, no action was taken thereon. Consequently, feeling aggrieved, petitioner has filed present writ petition before Allahabad High Court in the year 2000 seeking a writ of Mandamus commanding the respondents to provide her suitable post on compassionate ground. Honíble Apex Court in the case of Bhawani Prasad Sonkar Vs. Union of India and others reported in 2011 (4) SCC 209 has held as under: ì20. Thus, while c

reported in 2011 (4) SCC 209 has held as under: ì20. Thus, while considering a claim for employment on compassionate ground, the following factors have to be borne in mind: 2 (i) Compassionate employment cannot be made in the absence of rules or regulations issued by the Government or a public authority. The request is to be considered strictly in accordance with the governing scheme, and no discretion as such is left with any authority to make compassionate appointment dehors the scheme. (ii) An application for compassionate employment must be preferred without undue delay and has to be considered within a reasonable period of time. (iii) An appointment on compassionate ground is to meet the sudden crisis occurring in the family on account of the death or medical invalidation of the bread winner while in service. Therefore, compassionate employment cannot be granted as a matter of course by way
tail: mmediate help to the dependents of deceased employee, so that they may not die in starvation. It is settled position of law that compassionate appointment is not a Rule and cannot be sought, as a matter of right. The compassionate appointment is a concession and exception to public appointment provided under Articles 14 and 16 of the Constitution of India, therefore, to seek a concession of compassionate appointment, claimant must prove his financial condition and must prove that in the event of non grant of compassionate appointment, claimant would face financial crisis and may die in starvation. Since application seeking compassionate appointment was moved in the year 1996 and present petition is filed in the year 2000 and now, in the year 2014, when petitioner would have crossed the upper age limit to seek public appointment, writ of Mandamus commanding the respondents to provide compassionate appointment to the petitioner seems to be unjustified, at this stage. Therefore, relief sought cannot be granted at this stage. Consequently, writ petition fails and is dismissed. CLMA No. 8249 of 2012 as well as MCC No. 629 of 2012 also stand disposed of.
